### 2026-05-01T23:05:17.576Z Assistant [commentary]

I found the crash point: it’s in the TA `Course content` accordion header, not the video/player path. I’m patching that tile layout now so the week header uses a fixed-size leading icon box instead of a flexible widget that expands across the whole row.

### 2026-05-01T23:05:41.547Z Assistant [commentary]

The analyzer stayed green, which makes sense because this is a runtime layout issue. I’m making the week header icon box explicitly `48x48` so `ExpansionTile` gets a normal leading width and stops blowing up on narrow devices/emulators.

### 2026-05-01T23:06:32.532Z Assistant [final_answer]

Fixed the TA course-details crash in [D:\Graduation\EduVerse\edu_verse\lib\screens\ta\courses\ta_course_detail_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/ta/courses/ta_course_detail_screen.dart).

The issue was the `ExpansionTile` header in the TA `Course content` tab: its `leading` widget was using loose constraints, so on the MEMU width it expanded across the whole tile and `ListTile` failed layout. I changed that week icon box to an explicit `48x48` fixed-size leading widget, which is what `ExpansionTile` expects.

Verified with `flutter analyze lib/screens/ta/courses/ta_course_detail_screen.dart`.

Incorrect use of ParentDataWidget.
Competing ParentDataWidgets are providing parent data to the same RenderObject:
- Expanded(flex: 1), which writes ParentData of type FlexParentData, (typically placed directly inside a Flex widget)
- Expanded(flex: 1), which writes ParentData of type FlexParentData, (typically placed directly inside a Flex widget)
A RenderObject can receive parent data from multiple ParentDataWidgets, but the Type of ParentData must be unique to prevent one overwriting another.
Usually, this indicates that one or more of the offending ParentDataWidgets listed above isn't placed inside a dedicated compatible ancestor widget that it isn't sharing with another ParentDataWidget of the same type.
Otherwise, separating aspects of ParentData to prevent conflicts can be done using mixins, mixing them all in on the full ParentData Object, such as KeepAlive does with KeepAliveParentDataMixin.

### 2026-05-02T15:22:38.481Z Assistant [final_answer]

**Findings**

The root bug is real and systemic, but your suspicion needs one important correction: the exact `StateError (Bad state: Cannot emit new states after calling close)` on a fast back-navigation is mainly a **route-scoped cubit/bloc lifecycle bug**, not literally every cubit in the app.

What’s happening:
- A screen creates a local cubit/bloc, starts async work immediately, then the user pops the screen.
- Flutter disposes that local provider and calls `close()`.
- The async request finishes later and the cubit/bloc still calls `emit(...)`.
- That throws `Cannot emit new states after calling close`.

I audited the async state managers under `lib/bloc` and `lib/features`:
- `45` async blocs/cubits total
- `38` have async work with no real lifecycle protection
- only `7` even mention `isClosed`
- and among those, only [roster_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/roster/roster_cubit.dart:19) is using the guard pattern consistently

**Where the fast-back crash risk is highest**

These are the screens/features most likely to reproduce the exact error you described:

- Instructor assignments: the screen creates a local cubit and immediately loads data in [instructor_assignments_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/instructor/assignments/instructor_assignments_screen.dart:49), while the cubit has many awaited `emit(...)` paths in [instructor_assignments_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/instructor/instructor_assignments_cubit.dart:26).
- Student attendance: the screen creates a local cubit and fires two async calls immediately in [attendance_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/student/attendance/attendance_screen.dart:54), while [attendance_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/attendance/attendance_cubit.dart:17) emits after awaits with no close guard.
- Student lab detail: the screen creates a local cubit and chains follow-up loads with `.then(...)` in [lab_detail_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/student/lab_detail_screen.dart:38), and [lab_detail_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/lab_detail/lab_detail_cubit.dart:62) has multiple async emit paths.
- Student course detail: the screen owns and explicitly closes its local bloc in [course_details_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/student/course_details_screen.dart:202), while [course_detail_bloc.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/features/courses/bloc/course_detail/course_detail_bloc.dart:70) has many awaited emit paths.
- Instructor labs list: local cubit created in [instructor_labs_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/instructor/labs/instructor_labs_screen.dart:53), unsafe async emits in [instructor_labs_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/instructor/instructor_labs_cubit.dart:29).
- Instructor lab detail: local cubit plus `.then(...)` orchestration in [lab_detail_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/instructor/labs/lab_detail_screen.dart:59).
- Instructor attendance: local cubit in [attendance_manager_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/instructor/attendance/attendance_manager_screen.dart:27), unsafe async emit chains in [instructor_attendance_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/attendance/instructor_attendance_cubit.dart:26).
- TA attendance: same issue, because the TA screen also creates the instructor cubit in [ta_attendance_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/ta/attendance/ta_attendance_screen.dart:34).
- TA assignment submissions: local cubit created in [ta_assignment_submissions_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/ta/assignments/ta_assignment_submissions_screen.dart:31), unsafe async emits in [ta_assignment_submissions_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/ta/ta_assignment_submissions_cubit.dart:61).
- Student/instructor/TA calendars: all three use route-owned cubits in [calendar_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/student/calendar/calendar_screen.dart:24), [instructor_calendar_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/instructor/calendar/instructor_calendar_screen.dart:26), and [ta_calendar_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/ta/calendar/ta_calendar_screen.dart:55), and their cubits still emit after awaits without full protection.

**What is systemic, but less likely to fail on simple back-navigation**

These are still unsafe and should be hardened, but they are mostly **app-scoped** from [main.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/main.dart:181), so a normal screen pop usually won’t close them:

- Student assignments via [assignment_bloc.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/assignments/assignment_bloc.dart:61)
- Student course list via [courses_bloc.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/courses/courses_bloc.dart:106)
- Instructor course data via [instructor_courses_bloc.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/instructor/instructor_courses_bloc.dart:43)
- TA course data via [ta_courses_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/ta/ta_courses_cubit.dart:47)
- Student quizzes via [student_quiz_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/quiz/student_quiz_cubit.dart:20)
- Quiz management for instructor/TA via [quiz_management_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/quiz/quiz_management_cubit.dart:8)
- Notifications via [notification_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/notifications/notification_cubit.dart:47)
- Chat via [chat_bloc.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/chat/chat_bloc.dart:261)
- Discussions via [discussion_bloc.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/discussions/discussion_bloc.dart:63)

So your “all cubits” hypothesis is directionally right as a **code smell**, but for the exact fast-back crash, the main blast radius is the locally-owned academic screens.

**Extra architecture issues I found**

- TA attendance is using [InstructorAttendanceCubit](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/ta/attendance/ta_attendance_screen.dart:34), while a separate unused [ta_attendance_cubit.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/bloc/attendance/ta_attendance_cubit.dart:13) also exists. That duplication makes lifecycle bugs harder to reason about.
- Student attendance has both a global attendance cubit in [main.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/main.dart:189) and a local screen cubit in [attendance_screen.dart](D:/Graduation/EduVerse/edu_verse/lib/screens/student/attendance/attendance_screen.dart:54). That inconsistency is not the direct crash, but it increases maintenance risk.
- The `.then(...)` startup pattern in the lab detail screens is especially risky because it launches follow-up async work after the first future completes, with no ownership/lifecycle guard.

**Fix plan I would implement**

1. Fix the highest-risk route-owned features first.
These are the ones above: student course detail, student attendance, student lab detail, instructor assignments, instructor labs, instructor lab detail, instructor/TA attendance, TA assignment submissions, and all three calendar screens.

2. Apply the correct lifecycle guard pattern per state manager type.
- For `Cubit`: after every awaited call, check `if (isClosed) return;` before any further `emit(...)`.
- For `Bloc` event handlers: after every awaited call, check `if (emit.isDone) return;` before any further `emit(...)`.
- For stream/timer callbacks: check `isClosed` before `emit(...)` or `add(...)`.

3. Introduce shared safe helpers instead of hand-writing guards everywhere.
- A base cubit helper like `emitIfOpen(...)`
- A small bloc helper convention for `emit.isDone`
- This keeps the patch consistent across the codebase instead of becoming ad hoc

4. Remove risky `.then(...)` orchestration from screens.
- Move chained startup flows into a single guarded cubit/bloc method
- Example: instead of `loadLab(...).then((_) { loadInstructions(); loadSubmissions(); })`, create one guarded `initializeLabDetail(...)`

5. Add request-staleness protection for fast navigation and fast tab/course switching.
- Use request tokens or generation counters so stale responses are ignored
- This matters even when the cubit stays alive, because old requests can still overwrite newer state

6. Add real cancellation for route-owned network work.
- Pass `CancelToken` through Dio-based service calls for detail screens and heavy list screens
- Guards prevent the crash, but cancellation is better UX and reduces wasted work

7. Normalize ownership.
- Decide per feature whether it is app-scoped or route-scoped, not both
- Clean up cases like TA attendance and student attendance where lifecycle ownership is inconsistent

8. Add regression tests for “open then immediately back”.
- Widget tests for the route-owned screens
- Bloc/cubit tests that close the state manager before the delayed future resolves
- This is important because otherwise the bug will come back in another screen later

If this plan looks good, I’d start with the route-owned academic screens first, because that is where the user-visible crash is most likely happening right now, then I’d do a second pass on the global/shared managers.

- This is feasible.

**One important difference**

- Assignments have a file-delete API shaped around drive file deletion.
- Labs are modeled more around instruction records and their deletion flow is different.

not just a direct reuse of the assignment widget unchanged.

5. Preserve instructor and TA role behavior using the existing role-based lab editor flow.
6. Reuse the same UX pattern as assignments, but adapt deletion and existing-file handling to lab semantics.

- The lab editor save flow may need a cleaner way to expose the created/updated lab ID after save.
- If we want the exact same polished UX as assignments, we should also localize any new uploader copy from the start.

**Bottom line**

# Unified Role-Aware AI Assistant

## Summary
Build one shared AI assistant feature for student, instructor, and TA that visually matches the modern chat-detail experience, but runs on a dedicated AI architecture instead of the human-chat `ChatBloc`. Keep role-specific entry routes and colors, but replace the current three separate AI screens with one shared assistant shell, one shared message/composer system, one shared settings/history stack, and a provider-agnostic model layer that starts with Gemini and can expand later without rewriting the UI.

Key product defaults chosen:
- Chat history: local per-device, per-user, with manual export
- Model selection: global default plus per-conversation override
- API key source: local secure settings using `flutter_secure_storage`
- No backend changes
- Initial assistant scope: text-first AI assistant with role-aware quick actions and course/context scoping; no live voice or file-upload-to-model in v1

## Implementation Changes
### 1. Shared AI architecture
- Create a new frontend-only module under `lib/features/ai_assistant/` with clear separation:
  - `domain`: conversation, message, provider, model, role theme, context scope, export types
  - `data`: local persistence, Gemini provider adapter, settings storage, DTO mappers
  - `presentation`: shared assistant screen, widgets, bottom sheets, settings/history pages, role wrappers
- Do not build this on top of `ChatBloc` or socket chat services. Use a dedicated AI state layer so AI-specific features do not inherit human-chat behaviors like reply threads, delivery status, live typing sockets, call buttons, or participant logic.
- Keep current role routes, but point them to one shared screen wrapper:
  - student AI route
  - instructor AI route
  - TA AI route
  Each wrapper passes only role metadata and theme colors.

### 2. Provider/model system
- Add a provider-agnostic interface such as:
  - `AiProviderAdapter`
  - `AiModelDescriptor`
  - `AiGenerationRequest`
  - `AiGenerationResponse`
- Implement Gemini first using REST through existing `dio`, not the Dart Gemini SDK, so the app is easier to extend to more providers and avoids depending on an SDK that Google documents as not actively maintained for Dart/Flutter.
- Model catalog must support:
  - provider name
  - provider id
  - model id
  - display label
  - capability flags
  - enabled/disabled state
- Support global default model in AI settings and per-conversation override from the assistant screen.
- Show provider + model in the header subtitle and in the model picker sheet.

### 3. Local storage and conversation lifecycle
- Store API key in `flutter_secure_storage`.
- Store AI settings and current default model in `shared_preferences`.
- Store conversations locally as JSON files under app documents storage using `path_provider`, with a lightweight conversation index in `shared_preferences`.
- Persist:
  - conversation metadata
  - selected model override
  - role
  - timestamps
  - pinned/system starter prompts
  - full message history
- Add export/share for a conversation using existing share utilities; export format should be Markdown/plain text, not a backend sync format.
- Add safe handling for:
  - empty history
  - missing API key
  - provider error
  - rate-limit/network failure
  - partial stream/failure rollback
  - deleting a conversation
  - clearing the current conversation

### 4. Unified AI screen UX
- Use the current shared chat-detail screen as the visual reference, but build a dedicated AI screen with AI-specific behavior.
- Header:
  - constant assistant title such as `AI Assistant`
  - subtitle showing provider + model
  - role-colored modern hero/header treatment
  - replace call/video buttons with:
    - history button
    - settings/overflow button
  - include a compact model chip or model-switch trigger in the header area
- Message area:
  - keep modern chat bubbles and background rhythm
  - remove human-chat-only features such as reply-to, delivery checks, participant counts, live online status, and socket typing indicators
  - support system welcome cards and role-aware quick-start prompts
  - long-press on messages opens an AI-specific action sheet:
    - copy text
    - regenerate response
    - edit and resend prompt
    - delete message / delete from this point
    - share/export selected response
- Composer:
  - redesign the bottom bar for AI usage
  - remove irrelevant human-chat buttons
  - keep a clean text-first composer with:
    - prompt shortcuts button
    - context/scope button
    - send button
  - optional context chip row above the input for selected course/mode
- Add role-aware quick actions near the top or above the composer:
  - student: explain, summarize, study plan, practice questions
  - instructor: rubric help, announcement draft, feedback draft, lesson ideas
  - TA: grading help, clarification draft, office-hour support, summary help

### 5. Settings and subpages
- Add a dedicated AI settings page with modern role-aware styling:
  - API key management
  - default provider/model
  - response style defaults
  - local history controls
  - export/clear controls
- Add a conversation history page:
  - recent chats
  - pinned chats
  - rename/delete/export actions
- Use bottom sheets for:
  - model picker
  - message actions
  - context scope selection
- Keep UI responsive:
  - mobile: single-column conversational layout
  - tablet: constrained center column or split rail for history if space allows
  - no fixed-height areas that recreate the nested-scroll issues seen elsewhere

## Public Interfaces / Types
Add or standardize these frontend contracts:
- `AiAssistantRoleTheme`
- `AiProviderId` / `AiModelId`
- `AiModelDescriptor`
- `AiConversation`
- `AiMessage`
- `AiMessageAuthorType` (`user`, `assistant`, `system`)
- `AiConversationSettings`
- `AiContextScope`
- `AiProviderAdapter.generate(...)`
- `AiConversationRepository`
- `AiSettingsRepository`

Behavior contract:
- role routes must all open the same shared AI experience
- global default model is read first
- per-chat override takes precedence for that conversation only
- missing API key must route to a guided settings state, not a crash
- local conversations must survive app restart on the same device

## Test Plan
- Route coverage:
  - student, instructor, and TA AI entry routes all open the shared assistant with correct role colors
- Persistence:
  - conversation history survives restart
  - clearing one conversation does not clear all
  - exported conversation matches visible transcript
  - global default model persists
  - per-chat override persists for that conversation
  - API key is stored and loaded from secure storage
- UX behavior:
  - long-press actions appear on both user and assistant messages with the correct option set
  - model switch updates header/provider label immediately
  - quick actions create seeded prompts correctly
  - settings and history pages open and return without losing draft state
- Failure scenarios:
  - no API key
  - invalid API key
  - Gemini network error
  - provider timeout
  - empty message send blocked
  - deleting from a message onward updates local history correctly
- Responsive checks:
  - narrow mobile
  - large mobile
  - tablet portrait
  - tablet landscape
- Localization:
  - all new static text added to ARB files
  - no hardcoded English remains in AI assistant screens, sheets, or settings/history pages

## Assumptions
- Gemini is the only live provider in v1, but the architecture must not hardcode Gemini-specific UI or message formats outside the Gemini adapter.
- AI key storage in-app is acceptable for this prototype stage even though it is not the ideal production-security model.
- Existing role-specific AI screens will be replaced rather than maintained in parallel.
- v1 is text-first; voice-to-AI, image input, and attachment-to-model flows are intentionally deferred to avoid widening scope before the provider/model layer is stable.
</proposed_plan>

### 2026-05-03T18:41:37.342Z Assistant [final_answer]

Yes, the plan currently assumes compile-time injection like:

```powershell
flutter run --dart-define=AI_GEMINI_API_KEY=...
```

instead of putting the keys directly in a Dart file as constants.

Why I recommended `--dart-define` over hardcoded variables:

1. It keeps secrets out of repo-tracked code.
If keys live in a Dart file, they are much easier to accidentally commit, share, diff, or leak in screenshots and PRs.

2. It separates code from environment config.
The app logic stays the same across dev, staging, and production; only the injected values change.

3. It is easier to rotate keys.
If a key is revoked, you update the run/build config, not source files.

4. It scales better for CI/release builds.
Android/iOS release pipelines can inject different keys without editing code.

5. It is still compatible with a local private workflow.
You can keep the command in your own private script, IDE launch config, or local env wrapper, so you don’t type it every time.

That said, your alternative is valid too:

- `Option A`: `--dart-define` / build-time injected keys
  Best for cleaner architecture and safer team workflow.
- `Option B`: private local Dart config file ignored by git
  Easier for manual local development if you prefer “a place in code”.
- `Option C`: hardcoded tracked Dart constants
  Not recommended unless this is purely a throwaway prototype.

If you want, I can revise the plan to use `Option B` instead:
- a local file like `lib/config/ai_provider_keys.local.dart`
- imported by the app
- added to `.gitignore`
- with a checked-in example template file

That gives you the “put it in a file once” experience without making it repo-visible.

# Unified Role-Aware AI Assistant With Multi-Provider Model Support

## Summary
Build one shared AI assistant for student, instructor, and TA using a single modern chat-style UI based on the existing shared chat-detail experience, but powered by a dedicated AI frontend architecture instead of the human chat stack. Keep role-specific colors, entry points, quick actions, and context defaults, while replacing the current three separate AI screens with one shared assistant flow, one shared settings/history stack, and one provider-agnostic model layer.

Chosen defaults for v1:
- Chat history: local per-device, per-user, with manual export
- Model selection: global default plus per-conversation override
- App-owned provider keys: resolved from either a local ignored config file or `--dart-define`
- User BYOK: optional extra keys per provider, added by the user without exposing app-owned keys
- No backend changes
- Text-first AI assistant in v1; no voice-to-model or file-to-model upload in the first version

Provider plan for v1:

  - `domain`: provider ids, model ids, conversation/message entities, role theme, context scope, export types
  - `data`: provider adapters, local repositories, settings storage, app-key storage, user-key storage, DTO mappers
  - `presentation`: shared assistant screen, message widgets, model picker, settings/history pages, role wrappers
- Do not build on `ChatBloc` or socket chat services. Create a dedicated AI assistant state layer so AI does not inherit human-chat-only behaviors like reply threads, delivery state, participants, live online status, or call flows.
- Keep role routes, but point them to one shared AI assistant screen wrapper for student, instructor, and TA.

### 2. Provider/model layer
- Add a provider-agnostic contract:
  - `AiProviderAdapter`
  - `AiModelDescriptor`
  - `AiGenerationRequest`
  - `AiGenerationResponse`
  - `AiProviderCapabilities`
- Implement providers through REST with `dio`.
  - Gemini: official Gemini API over REST
  - Groq: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
  - OpenRouter: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Make the model catalog data-driven, with each model carrying:
  - provider id
  - model id
  - display label
  - free/free-plan flag
  - reasoning/tool/vision capability flags
  - status (`stable`, `preview`, `dynamic`)
- Support both:
  - global default model from AI settings
  - per-conversation model override from the assistant screen

### 3. Providers and free/free-plan models to include

- plus dynamic free-model discovery from OpenRouter’s live models API

Not in first coded batch:
- Cohere
- DeepSeek
- Hugging Face

### 4. Key management model
- Add two key layers per provider:
  - **App-owned key**: resolved from:
    1. local ignored config file
    2. or `--dart-define`
  - **User BYOK key**: optional user-supplied override, stored locally and privately on device
- Resolution order:
  1. user BYOK key if present and enabled
  2. app-owned key from local config file if present
  3. app-owned key from `--dart-define` if present
  4. provider unavailable state if none exist

Recommended implementation files:
- checked-in template:
  - `lib/config/ai_provider_keys.local.example.dart`
- local ignored file:
  - `lib/config/ai_provider_keys.local.dart`
- shared resolver:
  - `lib/config/ai_provider_keys.dart`

Behavior:
- `ai_provider_keys.dart` should safely import or reference the local config path pattern and merge it with `String.fromEnvironment(...)` values.
- Local file and `--dart-define` both remain supported.
- User settings must never reveal the app-owned key value from either source.
- User settings can only:
  - see whether a provider is “Available”
  - optionally add/replace/remove their own external key
  - optionally choose whether to use their own key for that provider

Important implementation note:
- because this remains a client app with no backend proxy, app-owned keys cannot be made truly secret against a determined attacker
- the plan should still hide them from normal users in the UI and avoid committing them into tracked source

### 5. Local storage and conversation lifecycle
- Store user BYOK keys in `flutter_secure_storage`
- Store AI settings and default model/provider in `shared_preferences`
- Store chat history locally as JSON files in app documents storage, with a lightweight conversation index in `shared_preferences`
- Persist:
  - conversation metadata
  - role
  - selected model override
  - timestamps
  - pinned/system starter prompts
  - full message history

  - TA: grading help, clarification draft, recap help, office-hour support

- Logic:
  - one active generation per conversation by default
  - disable send while generating or support an explicit `Stop generating` action
  - model change applies to future prompts, not the already-running request
  - cancel tokens or request ids must ignore stale responses after dispose/navigation
  - if user clears/deletes a conversation while generating, cancel request and prevent stale writes to storage
- UX:
  - show visible generating state
  - optional stop button while generating
  - no duplicate assistant messages from double-send

### 4. Message and transcript integrity
- Handle:
  - empty prompt
  - prompt too long
  - provider max-context overflow
  - export on empty conversation
  - deletion of a message in the middle of the transcript
  - regenerate last answer after prior error
- Logic:
  - trim input before send
  - block empty/whitespace-only prompts
  - if history exceeds safe context size, apply a predictable strategy:
    - keep recent turns
    - preserve system/context prompt
    - optionally summarize older turns later, but not required in v1
  - deleting from a message onward must update persisted history consistently
- UX:
  - clear validation feedback for empty input or oversized prompt
  - no silent truncation without user-visible behavior if meaningful content is dropped

### 5. Model catalog and provider selection edge cases
- Handle:
  - saved default model no longer exists
  - preview model removed by provider
  - OpenRouter free model disappears
  - provider returns unsupported-model error
  - user selects a model that requires capabilities unavailable in current request mode
- Logic:
  - fall back safely:
    - conversation override invalid -> provider default model
    - provider default invalid -> app global default
    - all invalid -> first available stable model for that provider
  - OpenRouter free catalog should refresh dynamically and invalidate stale selections gracefully
- UX:
  - show “model unavailable, switched to X” info banner when fallback happens
  - never crash due to stale saved model ids

### 6. Local storage and data corruption scenarios
- Handle:
  - corrupted conversation JSON
  - missing file in index
  - partial write due to app kill
  - secure storage read failure
  - shared_preferences missing/invalid values
- Logic:
  - use defensive parsing with fallback defaults
  - write conversations atomically where possible
  - if one conversation file is corrupted, isolate failure to that conversation only
  - rebuild index if possible from valid files
- UX:
  - show recoverable “conversation unavailable” state
  - allow deleting bad local conversation data from history screen
  - never block opening the assistant entirely because one stored chat is broken

### 7. Role, theme, and route consistency
- Handle:
  - wrong role wrapper passed to shared screen
  - missing role theme data
  - direct deep-link into history/settings/model picker
- Logic:
  - centralize role-to-theme mapping
  - provide a safe default theme if role metadata is incomplete
  - route guards must still open usable UI
- UX:
  - no mixed colors or broken header state
  - same interaction model across student/instructor/TA

### 8. Settings and BYOK scenarios
- Handle:
  - user pastes a key for a provider not yet implemented
  - user removes external key while it is active
  - user switches between app key and personal key
  - user clears all AI data
- Logic:
  - only implemented providers expose external-key controls
  - removing active BYOK immediately re-resolves to app-owned key if present
  - clear-all must define scope explicitly:
    - clear history
    - clear drafts
    - optionally clear BYOK keys only with explicit confirmation
- UX:
  - dangerous actions require confirmation
  - clear messaging between “clear history” and “remove my keys”

### 9. Security and privacy handling
- Do not log raw keys
- Do not render any key values in UI
- Do not include keys in exported conversation content
- Redact provider auth failures in user-facing messages
- If diagnostics are stored locally, store only sanitized provider error metadata

## Public Interfaces / Types
Add or standardize:
- `AiProviderId`
- `AiModelId`
- `AiModelDescriptor`
- `AiProviderConfig`
- `AiProviderCapabilities`
- `AiProviderCredentialState`
- `AiProviderError`
- `AiConversation`
- `AiMessage`
- `AiMessageAuthorType`

- `AiProviderAdapter.generate(...)`
- `AiProviderAdapter.listModels(...)`
- `AiProviderAdapter.validateCredentials(...)` where feasible

Behavior rules:
- global default model is used when a conversation has no override
- per-chat override takes precedence for that conversation
- user settings never expose app-owned keys
- user BYOK overrides app-owned key only when enabled for that provider
- OpenRouter free models remain partially dynamic
